Jamaat MP’s false claim on father’s 1971 martyrdom removed from parliament record
2026-06-21T17:08:43+06:00 | Star Online Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/the-parliament-watch/parliament/news/jamaat-mps-false-claim-fathers-1971-martyrdom-removed-parliament-record-4204326

Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad today expunged from the parliamentary record a controversial speech by Jamaat-e-Islami MP Abdul Muntakim, who claimed that his father had been martyred during the 1971 Liberation War. The claim was later found to be false, as his father is still alive.The Nilphamari-4 lawmaker made the claim during the budget discussion on June 14, identifying himself as the son of a martyred freedom fighter. His remarks later went viral on social media, drawing widespread criticism and strong reactions from various quarters.

The matter was raised in parliament today through a point of order by Kishoreganj-2 MP Md Jalal Uddin, who demanded that the “false statement” be struck from the official record.

Jalal Uddin argued that Muntakim’s father is still alive, making the claim misleading and unacceptable in parliamentary proceedings.

Responding to the issue, Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad said, “This is not a point of order. However, the concerned MP has already met me in my chamber and admitted it was a slip of tongue. He acknowledged his father is alive and accepted responsibility for the mistake. Since it was unintentional, the statement will be expunged.”
